inspection.method: Original PNG loaded directly, not a crop or prior modern output

facts.observation: Two horizontal parallel interfaces bound a thin unhatched film. Air is above the upper interface; glass is below the lower interface and enclosed by side and lower boundaries. Glass has separated pairs of diagonal material-shading strokes, not a lattice. Right-hand index labels identify air, film and glass at their respective heights.

At the left of the layered block, horizontal extension strokes align with the two film interfaces, and oppositely directed vertical arrowheads delimit their separation. The annotation h lies next to this film thickness, not the entire glass depth.

An incident ray slopes slightly right as it descends from air to the upper interface. An upward ray labelled 1 leaves that same upper interaction. The source does not mark the interface interaction with a named point. The ray slopes are schematic separation, not a labelled angle.

The incident path continues through the film to the lower interface. Ray 2 emerges upward from this lower interaction, crosses the upper interface and continues into air to the right of ray 1. The two emerging reflections are close and upward, not two unrelated illuminations.

A downward ray continues from the lower interaction into glass and terminates inside the outlined glass region. It is visible in the source and must not be omitted when illustrating reduced reflection.

textInterpretationNotPixelFacts: Candidate prose specifies normal incidence, air index below film index below glass index, wave 1 reflected at the upper boundary, wave 2 at the lower boundary, geometric round-trip distance 2h, and possible destructive interference.

The source rays are horizontally separated to distinguish paths. No incidence angle is given. Preserve this schematic convention and do not assert these displaced drawn rays are exactly perpendicular.
No sinusoidal wave, phase marker, numeric index, wavelength, quarter-wave equation, intensity or cancellation result is drawn in the PNG.
